h3_prompt:
Subject: Landscape 16:9, one continuous 11-second single-character narrative. Show exactly one physical instance of the established heavy adult adventurer from Picture 1. Preserve his broad heavy body, grounded weight, short dark hair, thick dark beard, tired experienced face, layered worn dark clothing, red scarf, crossing straps and buckles, pale metal shoulder and chest structure, complete backpack and rolled equipment, one cyan-lit waist lantern, heavy gloves and boots. Keep every connected item, body proportion, material, surface wear and reference color unchanged.

Movement: From 0 to 2 seconds he stands still with both boots planted and the complete load already settled. From 2 to 4 seconds one brief natural air movement crosses only the existing foliage or water surface visibly supported by Picture 2; it creates no new object and no danger. From 4 to 6 seconds only the existing loose edge of his scarf and the nearest attached cloth layer respond once, while his torso, boots and load remain grounded. From 6 to 8 seconds his eyes move first and his head turns only a few degrees toward the affected side, then stops. From 8 to 10 seconds one gloved hand makes a single small press on one already-existing chest strap; no buckle changes, no tightening cycle, no step and no repeated correction. From 10 to 11 seconds the hand and cloth stop, the load remains complete, and he holds a calm stable result.

Scene: Picture 2 defines SCENE-03, the same forest-lake environment, its existing elements, spatial continuity and original three-color foreground-middle-background hierarchy. Use the brief air movement only if the bound scene image visibly supports existing foliage or water. Do not invent a path, narrowing, obstacle, bridge, rock, root, building, sign, rail, creature, vehicle or new weather event.

Camera: One locked eye-level full-body medium-wide three-quarter view in a 16:9 landscape frame. Keep both boots, the full backpack silhouette, the existing strap touched by his hand and the supported scene layers readable together. Fixed framing, focal length and horizon; no push, pull, pan, tilt, tracking, reframing, cut, transition or split screen.

Lighting: Preserve Picture 1 materials and Picture 2 palette logic under one fixed soft diffuse light. Keep the cyan lantern as one small identity light only. No new glow, flashing, relighting, weather change, sudden saturation shift or color redesign.

Atmosphere: He should read as alert without alarm and experienced without theatricality. The appeal comes from noticing a small environmental change, checking it, and making one economical contact with equipment that was already correctly worn. Use clear two-dimensional hand-drawn shapes, restrained variable-width linework, soft diffuse depth and low-saturation shadows only where compatible with the bound references.

Audio: Ambient soundscape: quiet forest-lake air, distant water only if supported by Picture 2, one brief soft leaf-or-surface rustle, one cloth response, a faint existing-strap creak and low equipment weight. Emotional sound cue: one sparse non-melodic low tone rises slightly during the eye-and-head check and settles when the hand stops, with no lyrics and no strong beat. Audio supports spatial awareness, action readability and restrained emotion only; it does not drive cuts and is not music-video editing.

Negative: exactly one character and one physical body, no duplicate character, no second human figure, no split screen, no clone or mirror-double, no reflection person, no crowd, no NPC, no extra limbs, no text overlay, no watermark, no abrupt redesign, no young slim redesign, no removed backpack, no dropped equipment, no duplicate lantern, no new strap, no new buckle, no new weapon, no step, no repeated adjustment, no panic, no run, no jump, no acrobatics, no invented object or scene geometry, no camera movement, no cut, no transition, no weather change, no abrupt color shift, no lyrics, no strong beat, no MV editing, no glossy 3D rendering.
